sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `atomic`. [claim-atomic-product-identity]
- Canonical name: Atomic, published by Bastani, Inc., with `https://bastani.ai/` and `https://github.com/bastani-inc/atomic` as the checked first-party routes. [claim-atomic-product-identity]
- Current status: the repository was public, non-archived, and active at capture; the release list showed 0.9.13-alpha.1 and stable 0.9.12. [claim-atomic-repository-status] [claim-atomic-release-version]
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-09. [claim-atomic-product-identity]

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: Atomic is classified as a local terminal agent runtime with orchestration as a secondary role. [claim-atomic-primary-type-runtime] [claim-atomic-secondary-role-orchestrator]
- What it is not: its README says it is not a wrapper around Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Copilot CLI, and says direct chat fits small interactive work better than a tracked workflow. [claim-atomic-not-for]

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a project-taxonomy inference. [claim-atomic-primary-type-runtime]
- Agent-loop owner: Atomic `AgentSession` checks model, auth, extensions, and tools, then drives the underlying prompt loop. [claim-atomic-agent-loop-owner]
- Architecture: the `@bastani/atomic` coding-agent package exposes the `atomic` CLI and declares Pi agent, AI, and TUI dependencies; workflow stages and DBOS/Postgres-backed durable state are documented separately. [claim-atomic-package-architecture] [claim-atomic-orchestration] [claim-atomic-workflow-data-path]

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-atomic-cli`, `surface-atomic-print`, `surface-atomic-json`, `surface-atomic-rpc`, `surface-atomic-sdk`, `surface-atomic-workflow-tui`, and `surface-atomic-termux`. [claim-atomic-surface-cli] [claim-atomic-surface-print] [claim-atomic-surface-json] [claim-atomic-surface-rpc] [claim-atomic-surface-sdk] [claim-atomic-surface-workflow-tui] [claim-atomic-termux-route]
- Execution location: the default runtime executes locally from the current project directory in the invoking user's trust boundary. [claim-atomic-local-execution]
- Availability: the Quickstart documents global installation through npm, pnpm, or Bun. [claim-atomic-public-availability]

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: Atomic composes built-in catalogs, `models.json`, native provider APIs, and extension-registered providers; compaction documentation separately records fallback planning. [claim-atomic-model-strategy] [claim-atomic-compaction]
- Auth strategy: subscription OAuth, API keys, local auth storage, environment variables, models configuration, and extension-provided OAuth are documented; the local auth file is created with `0600` permissions. [claim-atomic-auth-strategy]
- Provider support: documented routes include Claude, Codex, Copilot, xAI subscription access, API-key/cloud providers, custom APIs, and local Ollama, LM Studio, or vLLM endpoints. [claim-atomic-provider-support] [claim-atomic-local-model-support]

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: sessions and workflow stages can use fresh or forked context and artifact-backed handoffs. [claim-atomic-context-behavior]
- Memory: transcript, branch, artifact, and durable run state are documented; a separate semantic/vector memory subsystem remains unknown. [claim-atomic-memory-boundary] [claim-atomic-semantic-memory-unknown]
- Compaction: Atomic documents local verbatim line-range compaction, optional fallback-model planning, and a fresh-context overflow rung. [claim-atomic-compaction]
- Session behavior: persistent JSONL session trees support resume, tree navigation, fork, clone, export, and workflow-stage resume. [claim-atomic-session-behavior]

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: the default coding set includes read, bash, edit, write, find, search, ask-user, and todo tools. [claim-atomic-built-in-tools]
- Extensions: trusted TypeScript modules can add tools, commands, providers, UI, and lifecycle behavior. [claim-atomic-extension-model]
- MCP: MCP tools and workflow-stage allow/deny scope are documented. [claim-atomic-mcp-support]
- Skills: Atomic implements Agent Skills and supports documented Claude Code and Codex skill directories. [claim-atomic-skills-support]
- Hooks: extension hooks span project trust, sessions, providers, models, input, and tool calls/results. [claim-atomic-hook-support]
- APIs: first-party SDK, JSON event stream, stdin/stdout RPC, and provider-registration APIs are documented. [claim-atomic-integration-apis]

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: TypeScript workflow graphs support stages, branches, artifacts, checks, gates, human input, nested workflows, retries, and resume. [claim-atomic-orchestration]
- Parallelism: workflows and subagents support bounded fan-out; documented subagent limits are configuration facts, not benchmark results. [claim-atomic-parallelism]

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: fresh/forked context and worktrees isolate context or checkout state, while bundled subagents run in-process. [claim-atomic-isolation-boundary] The security docs separately state that no OS sandbox is built in. [claim-atomic-no-sandbox-drawback]
- Permissions: tools, extensions, and shell commands run with the Atomic process user's permissions; tool lists reduce exposure but are not shell-command policy. [claim-atomic-permission-boundary]
- Security: project trust, private reporting, and external containment patterns are documented on the security page; owner-only local auth is documented on the providers page. [claim-atomic-security-boundary] [claim-atomic-auth-strategy]
- Data path: auth and session state are local under `~/.atomic/agent`; durable workflow state uses DBOS/Postgres and run-scoped artifacts. [claim-atomic-local-data-path] [claim-atomic-session-data-path] [claim-atomic-workflow-data-path]

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-cli` is the local interactive terminal/TUI with approvals, tool inspection, and local continuity. [claim-atomic-surface-cli]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-print` is single-shot and has no interactive approval UI. [claim-atomic-surface-print]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-json` is local JSONL event output, not a browser client. [claim-atomic-surface-json]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-rpc` is local stdin/stdout RPC. [claim-atomic-surface-rpc]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-sdk` is in-process integration, not a first-party app. [claim-atomic-surface-sdk]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-workflow-tui` is the terminal graph and attached-stage supervision route. [claim-atomic-surface-workflow-tui]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-atomic-termux` is same-device Android terminal use. [claim-atomic-termux-route]
- Remote behavior: headless remote-machine execution is documented, but first-party remote client, vendor relay, remote start, and remote resume remain unknown. [claim-atomic-remote-headless] [claim-atomic-remote-client-unknown] [claim-atomic-vendor-relay-unknown]
- Mobile behavior: Termux is documented; native iOS/Android graphical, mobile-web, and messaging routes remain unknown. [claim-atomic-termux-route] [claim-atomic-native-mobile-unknown] [claim-atomic-mobile-web-unknown] [claim-atomic-messaging-unknown]
- Background behavior: named workflows can run in the background and resume; cron-style scheduling remains unknown, and async subagents do not survive parent exit. [claim-atomic-background-workflows] [claim-atomic-scheduled-runs-unknown] [claim-atomic-async-subagent-lifetime-drawback]

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Atomic software pricing is unknown; provider costs remain external and provider-specific. [claim-atomic-pricing-unknown]
- License: the file states MIT terms plus a prominent-Atomic display condition above stated usage or revenue thresholds. [claim-atomic-license-terms]
- Maintenance: repository and release activity were recent at capture, and the security policy supports only the latest released version. [claim-atomic-repository-status] [claim-atomic-release-version] [claim-atomic-maintenance-signal]
- Lock-in: Pi-stack and cross-harness skill compatibility are documented, but workflow state, DBOS/Postgres use, provider routing, and migration cost preclude a simple lock-in verdict. [claim-atomic-pi-compatibility] [claim-atomic-workflow-data-path] [claim-atomic-pricing-unknown]

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: Atomic declares itself a Pi fork and separately adds workflow, subagent, verification, and durable-run behavior. [claim-atomic-pi-fork-lineage] [claim-atomic-extends-pi]
- Relationship edges: baseline `atomic --fork_of--> pi` is preserved and not recreated; this proposal adds no relationship tuple. Compatibility and added behavior remain claims, not an `extends` edge. [claim-atomic-pi-fork-lineage] [claim-atomic-extends-pi]

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `neighborhood-pi-lineage-terminal-runtimes`. [claim-atomic-lineage-neighborhood]
- Substitutes: unknown; Pi lineage does not prove interchangeable workflows or security behavior. [claim-atomic-lineage-neighborhood]
- Partial substitutes: unknown pending user-job and operating-model evidence beyond lineage. [claim-atomic-lineage-neighborhood]
- Same-lineage relatives: Pi, Oh My Pi, and Prime Agent; Atomic's decisive difference is its documented versioned workflow and durable orchestration layer. [claim-atomic-lineage-neighborhood] [claim-atomic-orchestration] [claim-atomic-durable-workflows]
- Often-confused products: wrapper CLIs are explicitly not Atomic's claimed product model. [claim-atomic-not-for]
- Complements: unknown within the eligible Wave 1 neighborhood set; the separate workflow registry was not used to form a cross-Wave-1-product neighborhood. [claim-atomic-lineage-neighborhood]

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: an inference identifies the combination of Pi lineage, versioned workflow graphs, checks, artifacts, fresh-context verification, human gates, and durable replay. [claim-atomic-unique-value]
- Meaningful drawbacks: no built-in OS sandbox, fallback compaction may route transcript context to another provider, and async subagents have parent-process lifetime. [claim-atomic-no-sandbox-drawback] [claim-atomic-fallback-data-path-drawback] [claim-atomic-async-subagent-lifetime-drawback]
- Best fit: an inference points to engineers who need repeatable multi-stage work, artifacts, review, approvals, or resumable background execution. [claim-atomic-intended-user]
- Not-for: the vendor points small interactive work to direct chat and says Atomic is not a wrapper around another vendor CLI. [claim-atomic-not-for]

claims.claim: Atomic's Quickstart documents global installation with npm, pnpm, or Bun.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-availability. BF-01 narrows this record to methods stated on the cited page. No install was run.

claims.claim: The release list showed 0.9.13-alpha.1 as newest and 0.9.12 as newest stable.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-release-version. Updated by claim-atomic-gf-atomic-ver-0914a1 (gap-fill 2026-08-16, Maria-adjudicated).

claims.claim: A first-party desktop or browser client attaching to a remote Atomic backend was not established.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: inference. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-remote-client-unknown.

claims.claim: Atomic documents running its CLI or RPC process on a headless or remote machine, with manual auth-code entry where supported.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-remote-headless.

claims.claim: The Atomic repository was public, non-archived, non-disabled, and showed a same-day push and update.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-status.

claims.claim: Cron-style or scheduler-driven first-party runs were not established, although background resumable workflows are documented.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: inference. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-scheduled-unknown.

claims.claim: Atomic has orchestration as a secondary role through its workflow layer.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-secondary-orchestrator.

claims.claim: Atomic documents project trust, private vulnerability reporting, and external containment patterns.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-security. BF-04 moves the 0600 auth-file fact to claim-atomic-auth-strategy.

claims.claim: A separate long-term semantic or vector-memory subsystem was not established.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: inference. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-semantic-memory-unknown.

claims.claim: Atomic persists JSONL session trees and supports resume, tree navigation, fork, clone, compact, and export.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-sessions.

claims.claim: Persistent sessions are JSONL files under ~/.atomic/agent/sessions by default, with custom directory options.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-session-data-path.

claims.claim: Atomic implements Agent Skills and supports documented Claude Code and Codex skill directories.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-skills.

claims.claim: Atomic's interactive terminal/TUI supports local chat, tools, sessions, workflow commands, inspection, and human input.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-surface-cli.

claims.claim: Atomic has a local JSONL event-stream CLI mode with session, message, tool, model, and compaction events.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-surface-json.

claims.claim: Atomic print mode sends one prompt, prints the result, and exits without an interactive UI gate.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-surface-print.

claims.claim: Atomic has a local stdin/stdout JSONL RPC process interface.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-surface-rpc.

claims.claim: Atomic has an in-process SDK for integrator-built interfaces.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-surface-sdk. It is not itself a first-party app.

claims.claim: Atomic's workflow graph and attached-stage chat provide terminal inspection, steering, human input, pause, and resume controls.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-surface-workflow-tui.

claims.claim: Atomic documents same-device Android Termux use and says no native Android ARM64 target is available.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-mobile-termux.

claims.claim: Inference: Atomic's distinct cohort combination is Pi lineage plus versioned graphs, checks, artifacts, fresh-context verification, gates, and durable replay.
claims.value: Pi-lineage runtime with durable verified workflow graphs
claims.notes: Assertion kind: inference. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-unique-value.

claims.claim: A vendor-operated Atomic relay was not established.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: inference. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-relay-unknown.

claims.claim: Durable workflows use DBOS/Postgres and run-scoped artifacts under ~/.atomic/workflows/runs/<runId>/.
claims.notes: Assertion kind: fact. Source evidence item: claim-atomic-wave3-workflow-data-path.
